subject: Constantin Brâncuși (1876–1957), Romanian sculptor, photographed by Edward Steichen in 1922. Per the Wikimedia Commons primary record (re-fetched 2026-05-02), the location is 'Brâncuşi's workshop in Voulangis, France' — i.e., a workshop set up at Steichen's country home in Voulangis, France, where Brâncuşi visited and worked. (Distinguish from Steichen's separate 1925 portrait Brancusi in His Studio, Paris, which is documented at Brâncuşi's own Paris studio per src-aperture-prints-brancusi-1925.) The photograph anchors the Steichen-Brâncuşi friendship that would lead to the 1928 Brancusi v. United States customs case. PD-US-expired status applies for U.S. distribution; per the Commons warning the image may not be in the public domain outside the United States — countries that do not apply the rule of the shorter term to US works (Canada, mainland China, Germany, Mexico, Switzerland) may still treat the photograph as under copyright until Steichen's life+70 expires (2043).
